title: Set up Kaggle access and reproducible download script
body: Every member creates a Kaggle account, accepts the IEEE-CIS competition rules, and generates an API token. Leonel writes `scripts/setup_data.py` to pull the files, verify integrity, and fail on a truncated download.

title: Define repo structure and module contracts
body: Agree on the `src/` layout and the signatures for `load_data`, the feature functions, and `evaluate`, so the pipeline, feature, and evaluation tracks can be built in parallel.

title: Request GitHub Projects board and create September Issues
body: Ask the AI Studio Coach to create the board, then open an Issue for each task in the September plan, attach it to the September Milestone, and set initial statuses.

title: Merge transaction and identity tables
body: Join on `TransactionID`, decide join type, add a `has_identity` flag, and document the null convention. Identity covers only about 144,000 of 590,540 transactions, so missingness is itself informative.

title: Memory-optimize and publish canonical dataset
body: Downcast numerics, convert categoricals, and write a single Parquet file to the shared Drive folder so every member loads identical data in seconds rather than minutes.

title: Create and freeze the chronological split
body: Derive a day index from `TransactionDT`; split train days 0 to 121, validation 122 to 151, blind test 152 to 182; commit three CSV files of `TransactionID` values with a README. Blind test stays sealed until November.

title: Build the shared evaluation module
body: One function returning AUPRC, fraud recall, precision, F1, false positive rate, recall at 1% and 5% review rates, and KS. Every model in the project calls this and nobody computes metrics by hand.

title: Missing value analysis across all 434 columns
body: Quantify missingness by column and column group, and test whether missingness itself correlates with the fraud label.

title: Stand up the results registry and run conventions
body: An append-only log capturing model, feature set version, hyperparameters, split identifier, seed, and the full metric set for every run, so results stay reconstructible in November.

title: Categorical cardinality and distribution EDA
body: Profile ProductCD, card1 through card6, the email domain fields, M1 through M9, DeviceType, and DeviceInfo, and hand the findings to the encoding task.

title: Define encoding strategy for categorical variables
body: Choose per-field encoding, including grouping for the high-cardinality DeviceInfo field, and implement it as a reusable module fitted on the training split only.

title: Fraud dollar capture table and standard plots
body: Rank transactions by predicted risk into top 1%, 5%, 10%, and 20% buckets and report both fraud case share and fraud dollar share. Add shared PR curve, confusion matrix, and score distribution plots.

title: Business objective, assumptions, and evaluation framework write-up
body: Document the binary target definition, the cost asymmetry between a false positive and a missed fraud, and the review rate a real fraud operations team could absorb.

title: Literature and prior approach review
body: Summarize published IEEE-CIS approaches and the leakage traps reported in them, and bring open questions to the biweekly check-in with the Challenge Advisor.

title: Entity grouping feasibility investigation
body: Determine whether a stable card or user identifier can be built from card1, addr1, and the D columns. The answer decides whether the optional temporal and sequence work in October is possible at all.

title: Class imbalance and temporal drift analysis
body: Visualize the roughly 3.5% fraud rate, then test whether fraud rate and key feature distributions shift across the six-month window. This validates the chronological split and feeds November robustness work.

title: Baseline: logistic regression and random forest
body: First models through the shared pipeline and evaluation module. Sets the performance floor every later model must clear.

title: Baseline: LightGBM
body: Gradient boosted baseline on the agreed feature set, logged to the results registry.

title: Baseline: XGBoost
body: Gradient boosted baseline with class imbalance handling, logged to the results registry.

title: Baseline: CatBoost
body: Gradient boosted baseline using native categorical handling, logged to the results registry.

title: Milestone review and October handoff
body: Compare all baselines from the registry on identical validation data, agree the strongest configuration, and confirm scope for the October deep learning milestone.
